case_title.reason: Matches the judgment's caption: Suresh Kumar v. State of Haryana.

number_of_accused.reason: Only the appellant's liability is decided; the mother's leave to appeal was refused.

accused_gender.reason: Accused is the husband, referred to with male pronouns and as 'his'.

accused_age.reason: No age of the accused is stated in the judgment.

accused_religion.reason: No religious identity of the accused is described.

accused_caste.reason: No caste or community of the accused is named.

accused_occupation.reason: Judgment states the accused was in the Army and stayed home only on leave.

accused_socioeconomic_status.reason: No statement on the accused's wealth or class appears.

victim_gender.reason: Victim is the wife, Sulochana, a female.

victim_caste.reason: No caste of the victim is named.

victim_religion.reason: No religious identity of the victim is described.

accused_victim_relationship.reason: Accused was the husband; marriage on 18 February 1990 is stated.

offence_category.reason: Conviction is for dowry death under s.304-B IPC.

statutory_provisions.reason: Charges under ss.304-B and 498-A IPC match the judgment.

weapon.reason: No weapon is involved; death was alleged electrocution.

evidence_type.reason: Oral testimony, FIR, s.313 statements and absent doctor evidence are all discussed.

confession.reason: No confession or admission by the accused is recorded.

aggravating_circumstances.reason: Dowry demand, beating, short marriage span and cruelty before death are all noted.

mitigating_circumstances.reason: No mitigating facts are noted in the judgment.

trial_court_outcome.reason: Trial court acquitted, holding the death accidental and outside s.304-B.

high_court_outcome.reason: High Court reversed acquittal and convicted under ss.304-B and 498-A with stated sentences.

final_outcome.reason: Supreme Court dismissed the appeal, upholding the conviction.

offence_finally_established.reason: Both dowry death under s.304-B and cruelty under s.498-A are upheld.

imprisonment_years.reason: Seven years under s.304-B is the principal sentence; s.498-A term of three years runs concurrently.

fine_rs.reason: Fine of Rs.5,000 is stated for the s.498-A offence.

neutral_facts.correct_value: Summary of about 150-300 words describing only the incident, investigation and evidence, without reference to the section 313 statement (a trial-stage step).
neutral_facts.quote: the accused did not mention electrocution in his statement under section 313 of the Code of Criminal Procedure
neutral_facts.reason: Summary runs over 300 words and refers to the trial-stage s.313 statement, which strays from the incident and evidence.

offence_severity.reason: Judgment quotes s.304-B(2): minimum seven years, may extend to life imprisonment.

attempt_completion.reason: The victim died, so the offence is completed.

physical_harm.reason: Death alleged by electrocution, held not a normal circumstance, is recorded.

financial_property_loss.reason: No property or money loss is involved; the dowry demand was not a loss.

premeditation_planning.reason: Judgment does not discuss premeditation or planning.

motive.reason: Court accepted that the accused demanded a motorcycle as dowry.

key_evidence_accepted.reason: Para 49 lists the accepted witnesses and the cruelty and timing findings.

witness_credibility.reason: Trial court discarded Gian Singh; higher courts accepted dowry-demand evidence; electrocution theory came from a non-testifying witness.

post_offence_conduct.reason: The court makes no finding on the accused's post-offence conduct.

custody_duration.reason: Arrest on 19 September 1993 is stated; total custody duration is not given.

bail_history.reason: Supreme Court cancelled the bail bond and ordered custody to serve the sentence.

trial_duration.reason: All listed dates (death 16 Sept 1993, trial 3 Oct 1996, HC 25 Mar 2008, SC 11 Nov 2013) match the judgment.

legal_representation.reason: Counsel names for appellant and respondent match the judgment's appearance list.

investigation_status.correct_value: FIR registered 19 September 1993; accused arrested 19 September 1993; tried; trial completed
investigation_status.quote: Pursuant to the investigation carried out by the police, Suresh Kumar was arrested on the same day
investigation_status.reason: Charge-sheet filing is not stated in the judgment; the 'charge-sheeted' claim is unsupported.

procedural_irregularity.reason: FIR delay was raised first in the Supreme Court and rejected; no other irregularity is noted.

appeal_history.reason: Trial acquittal, High Court reversal and Supreme Court dismissal are correctly stated.

prosecution_argument.reason: The judgment records no State submissions in the Supreme Court, so 'Not stated' is accurate.

defence_argument.reason: All four defence contentions (merits, interference, accident, doctor, FIR delay) appear in the judgment.

legal_principle_applied.reason: Two-stage s.304-B/113-B process, accidental death within s.304-B, and jurisdictional-error interference are all stated.
